units.title: Introduction to Income Tax Act 1961 and Important Concept under the Act
units.topics: Tax: Meaning, concept and objectives Income Tax Act -1961- Concepts, Meaning and Definitions, Indian Tax System, Direct Tax and Indirect Tax, Difference between Direct Tax and Indirect Tax, canon of taxation, Residential status & tax incidence, Income exempt from tax. Definitions: Income, Person, Assessee, Deemed Assessee, Assessment year, Pervious year, Agricultural Income, Exempted Income, Gross Total Income (GTI), Total Taxable Income (TTI), Residential Status of an Assessee, PAN, TAN, Recent reforms in Direct Tax

units.title: Heads of Income and Computation of Income under various Heads
units.topics: I. Income from Salary: Concept of Salary, features, Components of salary, Allowances- fully taxable, partially taxable, fully exempted, Perquisites and their valuation, provident fund and its tax treatment, standard deductions, Computation of Income from salary (Theory and Simple Problems) II. Income from House Property: Meaning, Basis of chargeability, Gross Annual Value, Net Annual Value, Types of property- Self occupied, let out, and deemed to be let out property, municipal tax, unrealized rent, arrears in rent, vacancy period, Deductions u/s 24 (Theory and Simple Problems) III. Income from Profits and Gains of Business and Professions: Definition of business, profession, vocation, Income not taxable under the head Profits and gains of business or profession, Expenditures allowed and not allowed as deduction, Depreciation Methods of accounting (Theory and Simple Problems) IV. Income from Capital Gains: Meaning, Chargeability-definitions- Capital assets, transfer, cost of acquisition, Cost of Improvement, Short term and long-term capital gains and capital assets, cost inflation Index, Deductions allowed. (Theory only) V. Income from Other Sources: Meaning, Chargeability Method of

units.title: Computation of Gross Total Income and Net Taxable Income
units.topics: Gross total Income - Deductions u/s-80C, 80CCC to 80 U – Total Taxable Income, Income Tax calculation of Individual - (Rates/slabs applicable for respective Assessment year), Education cess and higher education cess, surcharge, Difference between old tax regime and new tax regime (calculation of tax payable as per old regime) Computation of Total Taxable Income (Simple Problems on old tax regime only)

units.title: Filing Online ITR and Other Important aspects of Income Tax Act 1961
units.topics: Due dates of filing return, E-filing of Income Tax Return (ITR), Types of ITR, (ITR-1 to ITR-5) and forms used (Form-16 & Form 26AS), advance tax, TDS (Tax deducted at source), Types of Assessment, AIR (Annual Information Return), SFT (Specified Financial Transactions), Tax Collection at Sources (TCS), Methods of Payment of Tax, (Theory Only)

units.title: Introduction to Advertising
units.topics: Advertising – Meaning, Definition, Nature, and Scope. Role and functions of advertising in modern business. Types of advertising: Product, Corporate, Social, B2B, Institutional, Rural, and Global. Advertising as an element of Marketing Communication. Structure, functions, and types of Advertising Agencies. Client-Agency Relationship: Selection, Compensation, and Conflict resolution.

units.title: Promotions and Integrated Marketing Communication
units.topics: Promotion: Meaning, objectives, and importance. Elements of the Promotion Mix: Advertising, Sales Promotion, Personal Selling, Public Relations, Direct Marketing. Integrated Marketing Communication (IMC): Concept, benefits, and process of implementation. Sales Promotion: Concept, consumer-oriented and trade-oriented sales promotion techniques. Digital and Social Media Promotions: Influencer marketing, content marketing, promotional events.

units.title: Advertising Planning & Creative Strategy
units.topics: Advertising Planning Process: Setting advertising objectives (DAGMAR model), Determining Advertising Budget: Methods of budgeting (Percentage of sales, Competitive parity, Objective and task method). Target Audience Analysis and Market Segmentation. Message Design and Creative Strategy: Meaning, components of an ad copy (Headline, Sub-headline, Body copy, Visuals, Slogan, Logo). Creative Appeals: Rational, Emotional, Moral, Fear, Humour, and Scarcity appeals. Media Planning and Strategy: Media types (Print, Television, Radio, Outdoor, Digital), Media scheduling strategies.

units.title: Advertising Evaluation and Regulation
units.topics: Importance of measuring advertising effectiveness. Methods of evaluation: Pre-testing (Concept testing, Consumer jury, Mechanical tests), Concurrent testing, Post-testing (Recall test, Recognition test, Attitude test). Digital advertising metrics: Impressions, Clicks, CTR, Conversions, Engagement rate. Regulation of Advertising in India: Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI) – Role and Code of Conduct. Legal and Ethical issues in advertising: Misleading advertisements, Surrogate advertising, Puffery, Comparative advertising, Gender stereotyping.

subjects.title: Human Resource management: Employee Recruitment and Record Management

units.title: Manpower Planning and Forecasting
units.topics: Definition, objectives, and significance of Human Resource Planning (HRP). Steps in the HRP process. Methods of forecasting HR demand and supply (Managerial Judgment, Delphi Technique, Ratio-Trend Analysis, Work Study Method). Factors influencing manpower planning (technological changes, market dynamics, demographic shifts). Job Analysis: Concept, purpose, and methods; Job Description and Job Specification.

units.title: Recruitment and Selection
units.topics: Recruitment: Concept, importance, and sources (Internal vs. External sources). Contemporary recruitment channels: E-recruitment, Social Media Hiring, Campus Placements, Walk-ins, Employee Referrals, and Recruitment Agencies. Selection Process: Steps in scientific selection (Screening, Application Blank, Selection Tests – Aptitude, Psychometric, Skill-based; Interviews – Structured, Unstructured, Behavioural, Panel). Reference and Background Verification; Medical Examination; Job Offer and Employment Contract.

units.title: Introduction to Employee Records and Documentation
units.topics: Employee Records: Meaning, purpose, and legal necessity. Types of employee records: Statutory (as per Factories Act, PF Act, ESIC Act, Minimum Wages Act, Gratuity Act) and Non-statutory (Personal files, Performance appraisal records, Training records, Grievance records). Documentation during Employee Lifecycle: Offer letter, Appointment letter, Joining report, Service book/file, Code of conduct acknowledgement, Probation clearance letter, Transfer/Promotion letters, Resignation, Exit interview form, Experience and Relieving certificate.

units.title: HR Information Systems and Digital Record Management
units.topics: Human Resource Information Systems (HRIS): Meaning, objectives, components, and benefits. Functions supported by HRIS: Attendance management, Payroll processing, Leave tracking, Performance tracking, and statutory compliance. Digital Employee Records: Electronic Document Management Systems (EDMS), Cloud-based HR software, and Data Security. Compliance, Confidentiality, and Data Privacy: Adherence to the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, and global standards (GDPR overview). Retention and disposal policy for physical and electronic HR records.

subjects.title: Agri Business Management: Banking Operation and Finance

units.title: Introduction to Agriculture Banking Operations and Finance
units.topics: Agricultural Finance Meaning, definition, nature and scope. Need, importance of agriculture finance. types of available agriculture finance Systems of Banking (Merchant banking, Virtual banking, Green banking Unit banking, Branch banking, Group Banking, Chain banking) Scope of banking operations and finance in India for modern agriculture and related business

units.title: Sources of Agriculture Finance
units.topics: Regional Rural Banks – origin, objectives and features; Micro-financial Institutions: Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) – meaning and features; Self Help Groups (SHGs) – meaning and features. Scale of finance and security for loans. Banking schemes for agricultural finance Differential Rate of Interest (DIR) Scheme – origin and features; Kisan Credit Card Scheme – origin, objectives and features. NPAs in agricultural lending: applicability of the SARFESI Act in agricultural lending. NABARD – genesis, objectives and functions; Insurance – meaning and definition. Crop Insurance Scheme – origin, meaning, importance and advantages of crop insurance, Comprehensive Crop Insurance Scheme (CCIS), National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS), Weather based Crop Insurance and Unified Package Insurance Scheme (UPIS).

units.title: Financial Management in Agribusiness
units.topics: Meaning, nature and scope of financial management in Agribusiness Difference between general financial management & agribusiness financial management Basics of Financial Planning in Agri Enterprises Factors affecting working capital in agriculture Cost-Benefit Analysis in Agriculture Role of RBI, IRDA, and SEBI in Agribusiness Financial Management

units.title: IT in Agriculture Banking
units.topics: Digital banking products: NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI Advantages and disadvantages. Online study of PM Fasal Bima Yojana. Introduction to IFFCO Kisan App, Agri Media Video App,Kisan Yojana,Mera mobile app, Crop Insurance Mobile App by Digital India. Introduction to Agri-Fintech startup farMart.

subjects.title: Service Management: Social Services & NGO Management

units.title: Introduction to Social Services
units.topics: 1.1 Definition, scope, and evolution of social services. 1.2 Typology of social services: Education, Healthcare, Child & Women Welfare, Elderly Care, and Poverty Alleviation. 1.3 Role of the State, Civil Society, and Corporate Sector in social services delivery. 1.4 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and their alignment with social sector initiatives.

units.title: Foundations of NGO Sector
units.topics: 2.1 Concept, meaning, and classification of NGOs/NPOs. 2.2 Legal frameworks for NGO registration in India: Societies Registration Act, 1860; Indian Trusts Act, 1882; Companies Act, 2013 (Section 8 Companies). 2.3 Tax exemptions and statutory compliances: 12A, 80G, and FCRA (Foreign Contribution Regulation Act). 2.4 Governance structure, roles of board members, and ethical leadership in NGOs.

units.title: NGO Management & Operations
units.topics: 3.1 Strategic planning for non-profits: Mission, Vision, and Program design. 3.2 Human Resource Management in NGOs: Managing full-time staff, volunteers, and community workers. 3.3 Financial Management: Sources of funding (Government grants, CSR funding, Philanthropy, Crowdfunding), Budgeting, and Financial reporting. 3.4 Project Management: Project formulation, Logical Framework Approach (LFA), and Resource mobilization.

units.title: Monitoring, Evaluation & Contemporary Issues
units.topics: 4.1 Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) frameworks: KPIs, Social Return on Investment (SROI), and Impact Assessment. 4.2 Accountability, transparency, and public reporting in NGOs. 4.3 Use of Technology in social services delivery and NGO management (MIS, digital fundraising, social media advocacy). 4.4 Emerging challenges: Sustainability, regulatory restrictions, professionalization of the social sector, and public trust.

units.title: Introduction to Banking
units.topics: 1.1 Meaning, Definition and Evolution of Banking in India 1.2 Structure of the Indian Banking System (RBI, Commercial Banks, Cooperative Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks) 1.3 Functions of Commercial Banks: Primary Functions (Accepting Deposits, Lending) and Secondary/Agency Functions 1.4 Principles of Bank Lending: Safety, Liquidity, Profitability, Diversification 1.5 Types of Bank Accounts and Customers (Individual, Joint, Partnership, Corporate, Minors)

units.title: Functions of Banks
units.topics: 2.1 Deposit Mobilization: Types of deposits (Demand, Savings, Term/Fixed, Recurring) and current schemes 2.2 Credit Facilities: Loans, Overdrafts, Cash Credit, Bill Discounting, Non-fund based facilities (Bank Guarantees, Letters of Credit) 2.3 Credit Appraisal Process: The 5 Cs of Credit (Character, Capacity, Capital, Collateral, Conditions) 2.4 Retail Banking vs. Corporate Banking: Scope, products, and target markets 2.5 Priority Sector Lending: RBI norms and significance for agriculture, MSMEs, education, housing

units.title: Banking Operations & Regulation
units.topics: 3.1 Role and Functions of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI): Monetary policy tools (Repo, Reverse Repo, CRR, SLR), Regulatory and Supervisory role 3.2 Prudential Norms: Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), Basel I, II, and III Framework overview 3.3 Asset Classification and Non-Performing Assets (NPAs): Meaning, classification (Substandard, Doubtful, Loss assets), Causes, Impact, and Resolution mechanisms (SARFAESI Act, IBC 2016, Debt Recovery Tribunals) 3.4 Know Your Customer (KYC) norms and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) guidelines 3.5 Banking Ombudsman Scheme: Purpose, jurisdiction, and dispute resolution process

units.title: Recent Trends in Banking
units.topics: 4.1 Digital Banking Channels: Internet banking, Mobile banking, ATMs, POS terminals, UPI, IMPS, RTGS, NEFT 4.2 Innovations in Banking: Core Banking Solutions (CBS), Open Banking, FinTech collaborations, Neo-banks 4.3 Risks in Modern Banking: Credit Risk, Market Risk, Operational Risk, Cyber Risk, and risk mitigation strategies 4.4 Financial Inclusion in India: Initiatives (PMJDY, Microfinance, SHG-Bank linkage program, Business Correspondents) 4.5 Green Banking and Sustainable Finance: Concepts, importance, and emerging practices in India

units.title: Introduction to Retailing and Retail Consumer Behavior
units.topics: 1.1 Introduction to Retailing: Meaning, definition, and nature of retailing; Functions and importance of retailers in the distribution channel; Evolution of retailing in India: Traditional vs. Organized retailing; Emerging retail scenario and drivers of retail growth in India. 1.2 Retail Formats: Classification of retail formats: Store-based (Department stores, Supermarkets, Hypermarkets, Discount stores, Convenience stores, Specialty stores) and Non-store-based (E-commerce, M-commerce, Direct selling, Vending machines); Concept of Omnichannel and Multichannel retailing.

units.title: Retail Customer Behaviour, Store Location and Pricing Strategies
units.topics: 2.1 Retail Consumer Behavior: Factors influencing retail shopper behavior (Cultural, Social, Personal, Psychological); Customer decision-making process in retail; Customer service in retailing: Customer satisfaction, loyalty programs, and retention strategies. 2.2 Retail Store Location & Layout: Importance of store location; Types of retail locations: Free-standing, strip centers, shopping malls, central business districts (CBD); Steps in selecting a store location; Store design and layout: Types of layouts (Grid, Racetrack, Freeform); Visual merchandising, atmospherics, and space planning. 2.3 Retail Pricing: Factors influencing retail pricing; Retail pricing strategies: Cost-oriented, Demand-oriented, Competitor-oriented; Mark-ups, mark-downs, everyday low pricing (EDLP), high-low pricing, psychological pricing.

units.title: Retail Operations, Merchandising & Supply Chain Management
units.topics: 3.1 Retail Merchandising: Concept, scope, and role of merchandising in retailing; Merchandise management process: Forecasting sales, developing assortment plans (breadth and depth), buying merchandise; Category Management: Concept, significance, and implementation process; Private labels/Store brands: Meaning, advantages, and growth in Indian retail. 3.2 Retail Supply Chain Management: Role of supply chain and logistics in retailing; Inventory management in retail: Stock-out risks, Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), Just-in-Time (JIT); Technology in retail SCM: Barcoding, RFID, EDI, Automated replenishment systems.

units.title: Modern and trending retail practices
units.topics: 4.1 Technology & Digital Retailing: E-tailing: Growth, business models, advantages, and challenges; Use of AI, AR/VR, Big Data, and IoT in retail operations and customer engagement; Self-checkout kiosks, digital wallets, and contactless payments; Quick Commerce (Q-commerce) and Social Commerce: Trends and operational dynamics. 4.2 Legal, Ethical & Global Issues in Retailing: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) policy in Indian retail (Single-brand and Multi-brand); Ethical issues: Predatory pricing, misleading promotions, consumer data privacy; Green retailing and sustainable packaging practices.

subjects.title: Human Resource Management: Cross - Cultural Human Resource and International Relations

units.title: Cross-Cultural Management & Global Business Environment
units.topics: 1.1 Concept of Culture: Definition, components, and characteristics of culture; Impact of culture on organizational behavior and workplace practices. 1.2 Cultural Dimensions Frameworks: Hofstede’s Cultural Dimensions Model; Trompenaars’ Cultural Dimensions; Kluckhohn and Strodtbeck’s Value Orientation Theory. 1.3 Cross-Cultural Communication: Styles of communication (High-context vs. Low-context cultures); Cross-cultural negotiations: strategies, tactics, and conflict resolution across cultures. 1.4 Cultural Diversity in the Workplace: Managing multicultural and cross-functional teams; Managing cultural transitions: Culture shock, reverse culture shock, and stages of cultural adaptation.

units.title: International Human Resource Management
units.topics: 2.1 International Human Resource Management (IHRM): Definition, scope, and differences between Domestic HRM and IHRM; Strategic IHRM: Aligning HR practices with global corporate strategy. 2.2 Global Staffing Approaches: Ethnocentric, Polycentric, Geocentric, and Regiocentric staffing policies; Managing Expatriates: Recruitment, selection criteria, pre-departure cross-cultural training, and orientation. 2.3 International Compensation: Components of expatriate compensation packages; The Balance Sheet Approach, Going Rate Approach, and Localization Approach; International taxation considerations. 2.4 International Performance Management & Repatriation: Challenges in evaluating expatriate performance; Repatriation process: Re-entry challenges, repatriation programs, and retaining returnees.

units.title: International Relations & Global Business Framework
units.topics: 3.1 Overview of International Relations: Concept, scope, and significance of international relations for global business; Geopolitics, sovereignty, and state-market relationships. 3.2 Global Governance & International Institutions: Role and impact on business of international bodies: United Nations (UN), World Trade Organization (WTO), International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Bank, and OECD. 3.3 Regional Trade Agreements & Economic Blocs: Overview of key regional groupings: European Union (EU), ASEAN, BRICS, SAARC, USMCA; Implications of trade blocs for multinational business operations. 3.4 Political Risk Management: Types of political risks (expropriation, nationalization, policy shifts, geopolitical conflicts); Methods of political risk assessment and risk mitigation strategies for multinational enterprises.

units.title: Industrial Relations & Labour Law Environment
units.topics: 4.1 International Labour Organization (ILO): Origin, structure, objectives, and Core Labour Standards; Impact of ILO conventions on national labour legislations and global supply chains. 4.2 Comparative Industrial Relations: Overview of industrial relations systems: Anglo-Saxon model, European (co-determination) model, and Asian models; Role of global trade unions and International Framework Agreements (IFAs). 4.3 Corporate Social Responsibility & Global Labour Standards: Ethical labour practices: Child labour, forced labour, occupational health and safety, non-discrimination; Supply chain compliance and codes of conduct in multinational enterprises. 4.4 Global Trends in Work and Employment: Cross-border remote work, digital nomads, and virtual teams; International mobility regulations, visa regimes, and immigration policies.

units.title: Introduction to Warehousing in Agriculture
units.topics: 1.1 Agriculture Warehousing: Meaning, definition, nature, and scope of warehousing in agribusiness; Historical evolution of agricultural warehousing in India. 1.2 Importance and Role of Warehousing: Role in reducing post-harvest losses, price stabilization, ensuring food security, and supporting the agricultural supply chain. 1.3 Types of Agricultural Warehouses: Public warehouses, private warehouses, bonded warehouses, cooperative warehouses, and cold storage units; Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) and State Warehousing Corporations (SWCs): Genesis, functions, and role. 1.4 Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA): Establishment, objectives, powers, and role in modernizing agricultural warehousing in India.

units.title: Warehouse Operations & Management
units.topics: 2.1 Warehouse Location and Design: Factors determining the location of agricultural warehouses; Design, layout, and structural specifications for scientific storage of agricultural commodities. 2.2 Storage Systems & Handling: Scientific storage practices for food grains, pulses, oilseeds, fruits, vegetables, and commercial crops; Material handling equipment in agricultural warehouses: Forklifts, pallet trucks, conveyors, and stackers. 2.3 Inventory Management in Warehousing: Inward and outward movement of commodities; Stock accounting, bin cards, ledger maintenance, and physical verification; Methods of inventory valuation (FIFO, LIFO, Weighted Average). 2.4 Quality Control & Preservation: Scientific preservation techniques: Aeration, fumigation, temperature control, and rodent/pest control; Sampling and grading of agricultural commodities; BIS and AGMARK standards for warehousing.

units.title: Post-Harvest Management & Technology
units.topics: 3.1 Post-Harvest Losses in Agriculture: Extent, causes, and economic impact of post-harvest losses in India; Strategies for prevention and minimization. 3.2 Cold Chain Infrastructure: Concept, components, and importance of cold chains for perishable agricultural commodities (fruits, vegetables, dairy, poultry); Cold storage technologies, pre-cooling, refrigerated transport, and pack-houses. 3.3 Modern Technology in Agri-Warehousing: Electronic Negotiable Warehouse Receipts (e-NWR): Concept, benefits, and operation through repositories (NeRL, CCRL); Automation and digitization in warehouses: Use of Barcodes, RFID, IoT sensors, and Warehouse Management Systems (WMS); Integration of agricultural warehouses with electronic National Agriculture Market (e-NAM). 3.4 Silos and Bulk Storage Systems: Modern bulk storage systems for grains; Metal silos vs. traditional bag storage: Advantages, operations, and maintenance.

units.title: Financial, Legal & Risk Management in Warehousing
units.topics: 4.1 Warehouse Receipt Financing: Meaning, process, and benefits of pledge financing against warehouse receipts (NWRs/e-NWRs); Role of commercial banks, RRBs, and NBFCs in agri-warehouse receipt financing. 4.2 Legal and Regulatory Framework: The Warehousing (Development and Regulation) Act, 2007: Salient features, rules, and regulations; Accreditation and registration process for warehouses under WDRA. 4.3 Risk Management & Insurance: Risks in agri-warehousing: Quality deterioration, theft, fire, pest infestation, natural calamities, and price volatility; Insurance policies for warehouses and stored goods: Standard fire and special perils policy, fidelity guarantee, burglary insurance. 4.4 Government Schemes and Public Policy: Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) sub-scheme under ISAM; Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) – Cold chain infrastructure component; PPP models and private sector investment in agricultural warehousing.

units.title: Introduction to Health Care Services
units.topics: 1.1 Healthcare Sector Overview: Definition, scope, and evolution of healthcare services; Healthcare delivery system in India: Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary healthcare; Public vs. Private healthcare sectors: Roles, infrastructure, and contributions; National Health Mission (NHM) and key public health initiatives in India. 1.2 Healthcare Institutions & Ecosystem: Types of healthcare facilities: Hospitals, diagnostic centers, nursing homes, clinics, wellness centers; Hospital classification: By ownership, size, specialty, and clinical systems; Medical tourism in India: Drivers, opportunities, and challenges.

units.title: Hospital & Health Care Operations Management
units.topics: 2.1 Hospital Organization & Administration: Organizational structure of a modern hospital; Roles and responsibilities of hospital administrators and department heads; Interdepartmental coordination and workflow management. 2.2 Clinical and Non-Clinical Services: Management of clinical services: Outpatient Department (OPD), Inpatient Department (IPD), Emergency/Casualty, ICU, Operation Theatres (OT); Supportive and non-clinical services: Pharmacy, Laboratory, Radiology, Dietary, Housekeeping, Central Sterile Supply Department (CSSD), and Biomedical Engineering. 2.3 Patient Flow & Facility Management: Patient registration, admission, transfer, and discharge procedures; Hospital design, zoning, safety, and disaster management protocols. 2.4 Biomedical Waste Management: Biomedical Waste (Management and Handling) Rules in India; Segregation, collection, treatment, and disposal of hospital waste.

units.title: Health Care Service Marketing & Human Resource Management
units.topics: 3.1 Healthcare Service Marketing: Concept, importance, and ethical dimensions of healthcare marketing; Designing healthcare service products and packages; Pricing strategies for healthcare services; Patient satisfaction, patient experience management, and grievance redressal systems; Branding, public relations, and community outreach programs for healthcare institutions. 3.2 Human Resource Management in Healthcare: Composition of healthcare workforce: Doctors, nurses, allied health professionals, administrative staff; Healthcare staff recruitment, credentialing, and privileging; Training and development in patient care, communication, and emotional intelligence; Managing occupational stress, burnout, and retention of healthcare professionals.

units.title: Finance, Legal & Emerging Trends in Health Care Management
units.topics: 4.1 Healthcare Financial Management: Costing of healthcare services: Cost centers, direct and indirect costs in hospitals; Hospital revenue streams: Cash patients, Corporate tie-ups, Insurance and TPAs; Health insurance in India: Government schemes (Ayushman Bharat – PM-JAY, state health schemes) and private health insurance; Third Party Administrators (TPAs) and cashless claim settlement processes. 4.2 Quality Accreditation & Regulatory Framework: Quality assurance in healthcare: Concept of medical audit and clinical governance; Accreditation standards: NABH (National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers) and JCI (Joint Commission International) overview; Key legal acts: Clinical Establishments Act, Consumer Protection Act in healthcare, PC-PNDT Act, Medical Negligence. 4.3 Technology and Emerging Trends: Hospital Information Systems (HIS) and Electronic Health Records (EHR); Telemedicine, digital health platforms, and remote patient monitoring; Artificial Intelligence and IoT in healthcare management; Home healthcare and preventive wellness: Growth and operational models.

units.title: Fundamentals of Innovation and Entrepreneurship
units.topics: Concept and Meaning of Entrepreneurship, Concept and Meaning of Enterprise, difference between Intrapreneurship and entrepreneur, Characteristics and Types of Entrepreneurs, Innovation: Meaning, Types, and Importance, Start-Up Ecosystem: Components and Stakeholders, Entrepreneurial Mindset and Creativity, Role of Entrepreneurship in Economic Development, Government Policies and Institutional Support for Start-Ups (State and central government initiatives)

units.title: Start-Up Creation and Business Planning
units.topics: Idea Generation and Opportunity Identification, Market Research and Feasibility Analysis, Business Model Development (Business Model Canvas), Preparing a Business Plan, Legal Structure and Registration of Start-Ups, Intellectual Property Rights (IPR): Patents, Trademarks, Copyrights, Lean Start-Up Methodology and MVP (Minimum Viable Product)

units.title: Start-Up Finance and Resource Management
units.topics: Sources of Finance for Start-Ups (Bootstrapping, Banks, NBFCs), Venture Capital, Angel Investment, and Crowd-Funding, Financial Planning and Budgeting for Start-Ups, Working Capital and Cash Flow Management, Costing, Pricing, and Break-Even Analysis, Risk Management and Insurance for Start-Ups, Government Schemes and Funding Support (Startup India, MSME, SIDBI, etc.), Legal and Ethical Issues Faced by Women Entrepreneurs, Case Studies of Successful Women Entrepreneurs

units.title: Managing Growth, Innovation, and Sustainability
units.topics: Scaling Up Strategies for Start-Ups, Digital Marketing and Branding for Start-Ups, Leadership, Team Building, and HR Issues in Start-Ups, Innovation Management and Continuous Improvement, Exit Strategies for Start-Ups (Acquisition, Merger, IPO), Sustainability and Social Entrepreneurship, Emerging Trends in Start-Ups (AI, FinTech, Green Start-Ups, HealthTech), Networking, Mentorship, and Incubators/Accelerators

units.title: Foundations of International Business and Core Concepts of Import–Export
units.topics: Introduction to the Meaning, Nature, and Scope of International Business, Domestic vs International Business. Understanding Globalization: Meaning, Benefits, Challenges, and Impact on Indian Business. International Trade Theories: Comparative Advantage, Heckscher–Ohlin, and Competitive Advantage of Nations. Modes of Entry into International Business: Exporting, Licensing, Franchising, Joint Ventures, FDI. International Institutions: their role in promoting trade: WTO, IMF, World Bank, and UNCTAD. India’s Foreign Trade Overview: India’s major exports & imports, Key trading partners, and Emerging trends in foreign trade.

units.title: Export–Import Process and Regulatory Framework
units.topics: Introduction to Export–Import: Meaning of export & import trade; Types of exports (Direct, Indirect, Deemed exports). Export Procedure: Registration (IEC, RCMC), Selection of product & market, Pricing & quotations (FOB, CIF, etc.), Processing export order, Pre-shipment and Post-shipment inspection and documentation. Import Procedure: Import license requirements, Placing an order, Opening of Letter of Credit, Customs clearance, Payment settlement. Export Payment Methods: Advance payment, Letter of Credit (LC) – simple mechanism, Documents against Payment (DP), Documents against Acceptance (DA). Export Incentives in India: Duty Drawback, MEIS/SEIS (or their updated equivalent schemes like RoDTEP), EPCG Scheme, and SEZ benefits. Logistics in Export–Import: Freight forwarding – basic idea, Incoterms (basic overview: FOB, CIF, EXW), Containerization, Marine insurance. Government Support Agencies: DGFT, FIEO, ECGC (Export Credit Guarantee Corporation) – their role in export promotion and risk coverage.

subjects.title: Community Engagement Program through Social Awareness
